releaseNotes: NChat 1.0.45 — voice messages, end to end. A recording now captures its real waveform (MediaRecorder's amplitude) instead of drawing a random animation, and that waveform travels with the message in thumbnail_url — the same field the web app reads — so a voice note keeps the shape of what was actually said on both clients, with the elapsed time counting up while it plays. The clip is written to the phone before anything is uploaded: a voice note recorded with no signal is queued with its audio and sent when the connection returns, instead of turning into a red bubble and asking for a second take, and its author can already play it from the device. Delivery is one path now, so a queued clip is uploaded at send time and the message posted behind it, and pause finally stops the microphone instead of only stopping the clock. Two wire bugs are fixed: voice notes replayed from the outbox were posted as type 'audio', which the web app does not recognise as a voice message — it rendered the media URL as text — they are 'voice' again; and a reply that was open when the mic was held is now carried on the voice note instead of being dropped. Failed sends say why in the server's own words rather than just 'not sent'.
